judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a direct pair of mappings and observed that the single-key result appears when pressing Ctrl+/. A maintainer can test the same precedence on a current build; the discussion's explanation has not resolved the reporter's follow-up that changing mapping order still failed.
evidence: The live body says the / key is mapped to the text '? ' and Ctrl+/ is mapped to the text '/'.
The reporter says Ctrl+/ still produces '? ' and later reports that changing mapping order did not resolve it.

A maintainer comment explains a possible precedence expectation, but the reporter's response leaves the observed behavior unresolved: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/35062#issuecomment-2374618039.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce both mappings on a current build and determine whether Keyboard Manager resolves the chord before the single-key mapping.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete fix attempt is linked. The current event-handling path is relevant, but the issue does not establish whether the result is intentional remapping precedence or a defect.

proposed_fixes.title: Resolve the Ctrl+/ chord before the single-key slash remap
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the single-key / remap may be consuming the physical slash key before the Ctrl+/ chord handler can apply its distinct output. This is not confirmed; keyboard layout and current-build behavior have not been tested.
plan: Recreate the two mappings on a current supported build and record the active keyboard layout and the exact virtual key captured for slash.
Trace Keyboard Manager's shortcut-versus-single-key dispatch for the matching physical key, including modifier state and injected-event suppression.
If the single-key mapping incorrectly wins over an exact chord, adjust precedence and add a focused engine test for overlapping single-key and chord mappings.
If chord precedence is intentional, document the supported ordering rather than changing engine behavior.
verification: With / mapped to '? ' and Ctrl+/ mapped to '/', confirm each input emits its own target text.
Repeat with mapping rows entered in both orders and confirm the result is deterministic.

confidence.rationale: The failure sequence is concrete, but a maintainer explanation and the reporter's contradictory follow-up leave the intended precedence and current behavior uncertain.

issue_context.summary: A single slash remap appears to override a separate Ctrl+/ remap, even after the reporter tried adding the chord first.
known_information: The single-key mapping sends the text '? ' and the Ctrl+/ mapping sends '/'.
The reporter says Ctrl+/ still emits '? ' and that another mapping order did not work.
inferences: Overlapping key and chord matching could explain the result, but the issue does not prove a dispatch-order defect.
The active keyboard layout could affect the virtual key captured for slash; no layout is stated.
issue_context.analysis: The report is sufficiently reproducible for a maintainer test and already contains a failed attempted workaround. Requesting generic logs would add little; the decisive question is whether a current build dispatches the chord before the single key.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue body and all four comments, including the maintainer's explanation and the reporter's mapping-order follow-up.

Checked the owning Keyboard Manager event-handler and shortcut mapping implementation in src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp and src/modules/keyboardmanager/common/MappingConfiguration.cpp; these establish relevant dispatch paths but not the cause.

reproduce.version_requirement: Use a current supported PowerToys build; the report used 0.84.1.
prerequisites: A text editor that displays literal typed text.
steps: Create a single-key mapping from / to the text '? ' (question mark followed by one space).
Create a shortcut mapping from Ctrl+/ to the text '/'.
Type / and confirm the single-key output.
Press Ctrl+/ and record the exact output.
Repeat after reversing the order in which the two mapping rows were created.
reproduce.expected: The single / input emits '? ' while Ctrl+/ emits '/', regardless of mapping-row creation order.

actions.label: Approve focused remap investigation
